title: One subsystem failing at startup must not take down the others
rule: In a startup or init function that sets up several independent parts (folders, settings, logging, the index), do not `?` the result of an optional part after the others are built. Keep its Result in the returned struct (or return it separately) and log it, so a newer-schema or locked index does not drop the settings store and the log guard. Make the field type `Result<_, ApiError>` so a later `?` does not compile silently.
rationale: E3.1 (#51): `startup::init` used `open_index(&paths)?` after logging started; an index from a newer app made init fail, and the desktop app then ran without its SettingsStore and log file.
